I was a chemistry undergrad and know a little bit about this. I remember doing a caffeine extraction, from tea, in an organic chemistry lab.

Yes and no. Caffeine is a water soluble drug, it's pretty easily extracted with hot water; however, for FULL extraction you would probably need to boil it for >30min. The issue, though, is you're also going to be extracting other compounds from the bean as well, some of which will probably be the cause of the added bitterness. A hot quick brewing process extracts a good portion of the quickly soluble caffeine and leaves behind less quickly soluble and undesirable compounds. Leaving it out overnight would definitely increase the caffiene content (though probably not significantly) but it's a process of diminishing returns. Plus what the other guy said, mold. Water + energy source (in this case coffee oils) = promised land for mold spores.

Caffeine is also degraded by the roasting process, if you're just looking for more caffeine, you could try switching to a light roast.
